test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 12 Nov, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following Census recorded negative population growth in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1921**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Census of 1921 is historically referred to as the **"Year of Great Divide"** in India.
 
• It marked the only instance of **negative population growth in India**, attributed to high mortality rates and epidemics.
 
• Factors responsible for this decline included widespread famines, the global influenza pandemic (1918-19), and other socio-economic disruptions.
 
• The population growth rate during the 1921 Census was recorded as **-0.31%**, the lowest ever in Indian history.
 
• After 1921, India witnessed consistent positive population growth in subsequent censuses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Census:** Conducted every 10 years, the Census provides vital demographic data such as population, literacy, sex ratio, and economic activity.
 
• **Year of Great Divide:** Refers to the pivotal shift in population trends in 1921, where India transitioned from fluctuating population growth to consistent positive growth thereafter.
 
• **Global Influenza Pandemic (1918-19):** Also known as the Spanish Flu, it caused millions of deaths worldwide, including a significant impact on India’s population during this period.
 
• **Factors Influencing Population Growth:** Population dynamics are affected by birth rates, death rates, migration, epidemics, and government policies.
 
• **Post-1921 Trends:** Following the 1921 Census, India saw steady population growth, fueled by improved healthcare, agricultural practices, and lower mortality rates.
